analysis_plan: Verify that the frozen teacher input has SHA-256 9a961a77628e365b54fdf59304ec7fddf46f1f4834c4c03cecea9c204f837f52 and contains exactly the two signed 784x50 and 50x10 FP32 matrices.
Report the teacher, mapped bounded-DRN validation, and fresh 10,000-example test accuracy, teacher agreement, teacher-student KL, selected layer fractions, fixed output gain, and conductance extrema.
Confirm that mapping performs zero optimizer updates and that every one of the 158,800 continuous FP32 conductances lies in [0.1020408197973068, 1.0].
Measure clean mapping loss before introducing IBM OM assignment, common-window contraction, HWA, or program-and-verify noise.

arms.description: Zero-update signed ReLU mapping into the bounded single-conductance FP32 DRN.
Fresh test evaluation of the exact mapped bounded-DRN checkpoint.

completion_criteria: The mapping arm performs exactly zero optimizer updates and saves one valid selected named checkpoint derived from the frozen teacher.
All 158,800 mapped values are finite FP32 conductances inside the declared bounds, with exact single-encoding halves/paired layouts and model-local amplification metadata.
A fresh completed evaluation covers all 10,000 MNIST test examples from the mapped checkpoint.

The mapped bounded DRN loses no more than 1.0 absolute percentage point of clean test accuracy relative to the frozen ReLU teacher; otherwise the direct-compression hypothesis is refuted and any later bounded FP32 distillation is declared as a separate intervention.
hypothesis: A signed 784-50-10 ReLU checkpoint can be compressed directly into the continuous bounded [0.1020408197973068, 1.0] four-device dual-rail DRN with no more than one percentage point of clean test-accuracy loss before any device programming.
motivation: Replace the independently trained 93.58-percent bounded DRN source with a function-preserving teacher-mapped FP32 baseline, while keeping exactly the conductance bounds and model-local amplification used by the IBM OM study.
title: Direct ReLU compression into the bounded FP32 DRN
